newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairies to see light rains as wheat heads.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairies to see light rains as wheat heads.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Friday were forecast to see light rains through to July 1 as wheat began heading across the southern grainbelt, officials said.

Central Alberta should see five mm (0.2 inch) of rain each day from Friday to Tuesday while Manitoba should be the driest area, only seeing five mm on Monday and Tuesday, Environment Canada meteorologist Francois Choquette said.

"Southern Alberta, southern Saskatchewan and southwest Manitoba (wheat) crops are heading now, further north it's tillering or jointing," said Bruce Burnett, weather analyst with the Canadian Wheat Board.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bu/ac but CWB cut them June 11 to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac due to dryness.
Spring wheat's heading stage is when its need for water is most accute.
A triangular area from Calgary to Lethbridge to Empress, Alberta, was rated very dry with the soil holding less than 30 percent of its optimum moisture capacity, Raddatz said.
All of southern Saskatchewan except for the southwestern districts around Maple Creek were rated dry with the soil holding less than 60 percent of optimum moisture capacity.
Southwest Manitoba was also rate dry, Raddatz added.
Soil moisture data was drawn from 160 Prairie stations on Monday June 23.
